svg.aria-label: Diagram: the google and google-beta Terraform providers, the four recommended Cloud Storage state bucket settings with Google's stated reason for each, the hundred-resource ceiling on a single state, and why the state bucket is a credential store
svg.title: Terraform on Google Cloud: two providers, the state bucket settings, and state as a secrets store
svg.text: The state file is a credential store that does not look like one
Every decision here is made in the first hour of a project, from a quickstart. None of them feel like architecture.
google
Provision and manage Google Cloud APIs.
Pin to a minor version: automatic patch upgrades,
while still keeping a solid target.
google-beta
Provision and manage Google Cloud beta APIs.
Chosen per resource, in the same configuration.
One extra line is how preview enters production.
The state bucket: four settings, each with a stated reason
versioning enabled
Earlier versions of the state are preserved in the bucket.
force_destroy = false
The bucket is not deleted if there are objects in it.
public_access_prevention
Contents are not accidentally exposed to the public.
uniform_bucket_level_access
Access by IAM permissions instead of access control lists.
The last two are post #22’s day-one policies meeting their first bucket — and UBLA is irreversible after 90 days.
State holds secrets, in plaintext
Many resources and data providers in Terraform store
secret values in plaintext in the state file.
Nobody chooses to put a private key in a bucket. It
arrives because a resource that generates one writes
its result to state, and state goes where you pointed it.
So the access model is a credential store’s
Only the build system and highly privileged
administrators should access the remote state bucket.
A developer who can read it to debug a plan can read
every secret the configuration has ever produced.
Grant it the way you grant Secret Manager.
Three defences, in order of how much they help
1. Keep secrets out. Reference Secret Manager rather than generating credentials as resources. Only defence
that removes the problem instead of containing it.
2. Restrict the bucket, through IAM under uniform bucket-level access.
3. Customer-supplied encryption keys — an added layer, over buckets already encrypted at rest.
The state boundary is the blast radius
No more than 100 resources in a single state, and
ideally only a few dozen. A modules directory and an
environments directory produce that split naturally.
State is not an inventory
Asset Inventory knows what is there. State knows what
was intended, at the last apply. The gap is drift, and
reconciling them needs both.
